step1_analysis.description: The circuit consists of multiple operational amplifiers with RC feedback networks, likely serving as a loop filter, error amplifier, or compensation network for an AC-coupled hybrid envelope modulator.

paper_reference.title: An AC-Coupled Hybrid Envelope Modulator for HSUPA Transmitters with 80% Modulator Efficiency

dc_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the active filter network.

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends on the RC ratios in the feedback network. Assuming standard 10k resistors, gain is typically around 0 dB to 20 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the closed-loop configuration of the op-amps.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * R * C). With 10k and 1pF, BW is ~15.9 MHz. Adjusted to match paper's 1.6MHz operating frequency.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The envelope modulator operates at 1.6MHz, so the filter bandwidth should be wide enough to pass the envelope signal.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifiers.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. Assuming 1.8V supply and ~1mA per amplifier.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical power for baseband active filters in 1.8V CMOS.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, AC frequency response, and transient response of the active filter network. Missing component values are parameterized with typical defaults.
